MIRRORS - INSPECTED, NOT SKIPPED (rule 10): the only mirror-type nodes on the site are /mirrors/ (h1 'Mirrors', 6 products) and its style re-cut /modern/mirrors/ (h1 'Modern Mirrors', 2 products). Under rules 2, 11 and 21 the primary product type is decorative mirror and the website hierarchy is Decor, so they route to Wall Decor / Home Accessories and are logged in `review` rather than fabricated into Bathroom. QTY (review rows only): Joybird listing pages are Next.js App Router pages carrying an Algolia InstantSearch blob (index products_jb4). For each of the two mirror nodes I took the rendered '<N> Products' header AND the blob's nbHits and required them to agree: /mirrors/ header 6 = nbHits 6; /modern/mirrors/ header 2 = nbHits 2. Each page's h1 matched the node requested ('Mirrors', 'Modern Mirrors'), so neither URL silently served a parent listing. This is the same dual-signal method the Furniture pass proved across 55 Joybird URLs. No count was estimated. Joybird is a Havenly-owned direct-to-consumer mid-century-modern FURNITURE brand (custom upholstery, case goods, outdoor, soft decor) and sells no sanitaryware, fixtures, bathroom furniture, bathroom mirrors, bathroom storage or bathroom accessories. Status is a confirmed absence, not an access failure: every request returned HTTP 200.
